name: Staffing Strategy
consequences: Hiring experienced research technicians will ensure safe and efficient monitoring operations, but may limit flexibility in adapting to unforeseen challenges.
options: Recruit and train local sleep lab staff for on-site management
Engage a third-party service provider for night shift coverage and event response
Develop an in-house training program for rotating research assistants
review: The proposed staffing strategies collectively do not resolve the risk of inadequate personnel to manage increased participant enrollment beyond 30–35 participants.

name: Participant Recruitment
consequences: Targeting specialist clinical interview referrals will yield high-quality participants, but may limit recruitment volume.
options: Expand recruitment channels to include online advertising and social media platforms
Establish partnerships with local sleep clinics for co-located participant screening
Implement a tiered referral system for general practitioners and primary care physicians
review: The proposed participant recruitment strategies collectively do not resolve the risk of inadequate control group matching.

name: Data Sharing
consequences: Public data sharing will facilitate collaboration and validation, but may compromise participant privacy.
options: Develop a de-identification protocol for public dataset release
Establish a secure data repository with restricted access for approved researchers
Create a data-sharing agreement template for collaborators to sign
review: The proposed data sharing strategies collectively do not resolve the risk of unauthorized data access.

name: Sensor Technology
consequences: Upgrading to higher-resolution sensors will improve data quality, but may increase equipment costs and technical complexity.
options: Replace existing dry-electrode EEG headbands with high-density arrays
Integrate ambient microphones with noise-cancellation algorithms for improved audio fidelity
Implement a hybrid sensing approach combining contact-free and contact-based modalities
review: The proposed sensor technology upgrades collectively do not resolve the risk of equipment obsolescence.

consequences: Developing a semi-automated event-triage tool will reduce manual review burden, but may compromise sensitivity and specificity.
options: Implement a machine-learning based approach for probable parasomnia episode ranking
Use a rule-based system combining multiple sensor features for event classification
Integrate a human-in-the-loop feedback mechanism for algorithm refinement
review: The proposed event-triage algorithm approaches collectively do not resolve the risk of inadequate algorithm validation.

review: The proposed publication strategies collectively do not resolve the risk of inadequate dissemination to key stakeholders.

name: Governance Structure

review: The proposed governance structures collectively do not resolve the risk of inadequate oversight during project expansion.

name: Participant Segmentation
consequences: Segmenting participants by parasomnia frequency can inform targeted recruitment strategies, but may inadvertently create a self-selection bias among higher-frequency participants.
options: Targeted outreach to high-frequency sleepwalkers through online forums and support groups
Recruit a balanced cohort of high- and low-frequency participants for more comprehensive phenotyping analysis
Implement an adaptive sampling strategy that adjusts participant recruitment based on real-time data from the residential unit
review: The potential for self-selection bias in high-frequency sleepwalkers could skew the sample towards those with more severe or treatment-resistant parasomnias, limiting generalizability.

name: Sensor Upgrades
consequences: Upgrading to higher-resolution sensors can improve data quality and capture rare events, but may also increase participant discomfort due to additional hardware.
options: Implement a phased sensor upgrade plan that prioritizes high-risk or high-reward features
Upgrade to higher-resolution sensors for all participants on the first night of each stay to maximize data quality
Develop novel, minimally-invasive sensor technologies that can be used in conjunction with existing equipment
review: The incremental cost and participant discomfort associated with upgrading to higher-resolution sensors may outweigh their benefits unless carefully managed.

name: Data Annotation
consequences: Automating data annotation can reduce manual review burden, but may compromise inter-rater reliability if not properly trained or validated.
options: Invest in machine learning-based annotation tools that learn from human annotators and improve over time
Develop a hybrid approach that combines automated annotation with human oversight for high-stakes decisions
Implement a tiered annotation system where simpler events are automatically scored, while more complex ones require human review
review: The trade-off between automation benefits and potential reliability costs may necessitate careful piloting or validation before widespread adoption.

Provide incentives or rewards for participants who complete longer stays or achieve specific milestones
review: The delicate balance between data quality and participant well-being may require iterative adjustments to the retention strategy.
